profiles.meeting_scenario: Nina and Omar are meeting to coordinate the handoff between a research prototype for sketch-to-code generation and a VS Code extension that will be used in an internal pilot next Tuesday with six researchers. The prototype comes from an exploratory study on ML sketches and visual code assistants, and the team now needs to align on what artifacts will be shared, how the extension will call the generation service, which model endpoint will be used for the pilot, and what counts as being ready to ship the pilot build. The agenda is to review current progress, confirm the interface between the generation service and the extension, align on the sketch dataset used for smoke testing, and agree on the deployment timeline. The expected outcome is a seemingly clear division of work for the next two days: Nina will provide the generation-side assets and examples, while Omar will wire the extension and telemetry for the pilot build.

members.name: Nina Park
members.expertise: Multimodal LLM prompting, notebook generation pipelines, evaluation for code generation
members.background: Nina built the research prototype that converts hand-drawn ML workflow sketches into Python notebooks and helped analyze outputs for the exploratory study.
members.private_state: She wants the internal pilot to preserve the behavior and quality seen in the study prototype, and she is trying to avoid any last-minute changes that could make the demo look worse than the paper results.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'the study sketches,' they mean the cleaned PNG exports that were manually curated and used in the experiment repository, not the raw capture files.
A 'notebook output' is a complete generated .ipynb artifact produced by the service, including setup, imports, markdown headings, and code cells in final order.
The 'staging model' should stay pinned to the multimodal checkpoint used for recent evaluation unless someone explicitly announces a version change.
Something is 'pilot-ready' if the end-to-end generation quality is acceptable on the canonical study tasks, even if a few retries or manual reruns are still needed behind the scenes.

members.name: Omar Haddad
members.expertise: VS Code extension development, telemetry, service integration, notebook UX
members.background: Omar owns the in-IDE extension layer and the internal demo infrastructure, and he has been adapting research prototypes into tools that can be used in live product-like environments.
members.private_state: He wants the pilot build to feel smooth in the IDE and to avoid brittle extension behavior during live usage, even if the generated code quality is still somewhat uneven.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to 'the study sketches,' they mean the raw files from the session-capture bucket, including screenshots and uncropped whiteboard photos saved during the experiment.

A 'notebook output' is the generated notebook content payload that the extension inserts into the user's currently open notebook, rather than a standalone .ipynb file replacing or creating a document.
The 'staging model' alias always points to the most recent deployed multimodal build, so using staging naturally means using whatever is current that day.
Something is 'pilot-ready' if the extension is stable, the round-trip feels responsive in normal use, and failures are rare enough that participants do not notice them during the session.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'study sketches' will be used for testing
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the study sketches' as the shared set for smoke tests and examples.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nina means the curated set of cleaned PNG sketch exports that were manually selected and normalized for the research experiment.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Omar means the raw session-capture files stored by the study tooling, including uncropped images and mixed file types produced during participant sessions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both artifact sets originate from the same study and are commonly talked about under the same label, so the phrase feels precise enough and neither expects the other to mean a different subset.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the service will return the 'notebook output' for the extension to show users.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nina means a full server-generated .ipynb notebook artifact with ordered cells, setup code, and markdown structure ready to open directly.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Omar means a payload of generated cells that the extension inserts into an already open notebook while preserving the user's current document and kernel context.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both interpretations are plausible in notebook tooling, and the shared phrase 'notebook output' sounds specific enough that neither feels a need to unpack the packaging boundary.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They casually agree to point the pilot flow at 'the staging model.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nina assumes staging refers to the pinned multimodal checkpoint that matched the latest internal evaluation results from last week.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Omar assumes staging is a floating alias that automatically resolves to the newest deployed multimodal model build.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Using a staging endpoint is routine infrastructure language, and both assume the deployment semantics are already shared organizational knowledge rather than something that needs restating.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say they want the integration to be 'pilot-ready' by Monday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Nina means the generated notebooks should be acceptably coherent on the canonical research sketches, even if a few requests need reruns or manual supervision before the session.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Omar means the extension experience should be reliably stable and fast enough for live use, even if some notebook contents are only rough outlines.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are sincerely talking about readiness for the same pilot, and each person's criterion is highly standard within their own role, so the phrase creates a strong illusion of alignment.
